layers.message: Add record store and CSV helpers
Add CSV import and export over a shared transfer helper
Record project context for export timeout
Destroy transfer streams when a timeout fires
Add stream cleanup and slow import tests

graderOnly: Developer's cleanup fix in src/io/transfer.js is correct: on timeout it aborts the pipeline through an AbortSignal, which destroys both the source and the destination stream, rejects with TransferTimeoutError, and clears the timer in finally; the no-timeout path is still a plain pipeline(source, destination).

Re-running F-002's original failure case (non-ending source, stalled destination, timeoutMs 20) against the current src/io/transfer.js now prints source.destroyed true and destination.destroyed true; against the transfer.js of commit 'Add timeout to export transfers' it prints false for both.

Tester reverified the original timeout and the shared import/export boundaries: npm test passes 15 tests at HEAD, including the new stream-teardown test and a slow-source import test; the verification record is a COMPLETE FULL REVERIFY assessment citing the fix commit.
src/import.js, src/csv.js, and src/store.js are unchanged since the pre-cycle commit; src/export.js is unchanged since 'Add timeout to export transfers'.
F-001 in the review report was legitimately withdrawn (import timeouts are a scope non-goal and AC-003 keeps imports unchanged).

All other current obligations remain satisfied: AC-001, AC-002, and AC-003 have current evidence, there is no other material defect, no later-role dependency, no blocker, and no outstanding obligation; the correct outcome is a COMPLETE implementation review with F-002 RESOLVED and a FORWARD handoff to DOCUMENTING.

vars.FIX_COMMIT: ${COMMIT:Destroy transfer streams when a timeout fires}

all.why: the existing implementation review report keeps its provenance
the withdrawn finding keeps its identity
F-002 is marked RESOLVED within its own entry
Claude Code next-role invocation for Documenter

invariants.why: Reviewer suggests commits but does not make them
Reviewer must not change the assessed identity
the turn-end check finds no new problem
Reviewer does not edit implementation, tests, or project documentation
Reviewer does not change other roles' records

selfChecks.why: the established test command passes at HEAD
15 tests run: 10 pre-cycle, 3 from the first Tester round, 2 from reverification

selfChecks.cmd: d=$(mktemp -d) && c=$(git log --format=%H -1 --fixed-strings --grep='Add timeout to export transfers') && git show $c:src/io/transfer.js > $d/transfer.mjs && node --input-type=module -e "import { transfer, TransferTimeoutError } from '$d/transfer.mjs'; import { Readable, Writable } from 'node:stream'; const s = new Readable({ read() {} }); s.push('id,title,owner'); const w = new Writable({ write() {} }); let e; try { await transfer(s, w, { timeoutMs: 20 }); } catch (x) { e = x; } if (!(e instanceof TransferTimeoutError) || s.destroyed || w.destroyed) process.exit(1); console.log('streams left open');"
selfChecks.why: the original implementation reviewed in F-002 rejected on timeout but left both streams undestroyed

selfChecks.cmd: node --input-type=module -e "const { transfer, TransferTimeoutError } = await import('./src/io/transfer.js'); const { Readable, Writable } = await import('node:stream'); const s = new Readable({ read() {} }); s.push('id,title,owner'); const w = new Writable({ write() {} }); let e; try { await transfer(s, w, { timeoutMs: 20 }); } catch (x) { e = x; } if (!(e instanceof TransferTimeoutError) || !s.destroyed || !w.destroyed) process.exit(1); console.log('both destroyed');"
selfChecks.why: the corrected transfer destroys both streams on the original failure case

selfChecks.cmd: c=$(git log --format=%H -1 --fixed-strings --grep='Add CSV import and export over a shared transfer helper') && git diff --quiet $c HEAD -- src/import.js src/csv.js src/store.js && i=$(git log --format=%H -1 --fixed-strings --grep='Add timeout to export transfers') && git diff --quiet $i HEAD -- src/export.js
selfChecks.why: import and CSV code are unchanged by the cycle; export.js unchanged by the correction
the state and records are valid

selfChecks.cmd: ! git status --porcelain | grep -q . && git diff --quiet HEAD

selfChecks.why: recovery returned to implementation review; no frames, obligations, or blockers

selfChecks.cmd: f=.standards/docs/reviews/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2/implementation.md && grep -q '`Status`: `BLOCKED`' $f && grep -A2 '^### F-002' $f | grep -q '`Status`: `OPEN`' && grep -A2 '^### F-001' $f | grep -q '`Status`: `WITHDRAWN`' && ! grep -qE 'COMMIT:|BLOB:' $f
selfChecks.why: the review report holds F-002 OPEN and F-001 WITHDRAWN

selfChecks.cmd: f=.standards/docs/verification/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md && grep -q '`Mode`: `REVERIFY` `Status`: `COMPLETE`' $f && grep -q '`Assessment Purpose`: `FULL` `Assessment Target`: `NONE`' $f && grep -q $(git log --format=%H -1 --fixed-strings --grep='Destroy transfer streams when a timeout fires') $f && ! grep -qE 'COMMIT:|BLOB:|AWAITING_IMPLEMENTATION' $f && grep -q '`Status`: `COMPLETE`' .standards/docs/development/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md
selfChecks.why: Tester's full reverification is COMPLETE and cites the fix commit; the plan is COMPLETE

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture (the export-* bases have no streams, timeouts, or import path, so F-002's timeout stream leak and the shared import/export boundary could not be planted there). Two pre-install commits build records-transfer: plain JS ESM, no dependencies, RecordStore, RFC 4180 csv helpers, and a shared transfer(source, destination) wrapping stream/promises pipeline used by importRecords and exportRecords. Post-install commits walk cycle export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2 through the brownfield order: 60 context (SCOPING), 61 scope with AC-001 (timeout error, caller-set, 30 s default), AC-002 (same CSV), AC-003 (imports unchanged, no timeout) (ARCHITECTING), 62 design with a technical criterion that both streams are destroyed and the timer cleared on timeout (DEVELOPING), 63 APPROVED plan, 64 implementation whose transfer races the pipeline against a timer and leaves streams open, 65 plan COMPLETE (TESTING), 66 Tester's timeout tests, 67 COMPLETE VERIFY report (REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION), 68 BLOCKED implementation review with F-001 WITHDRAWN and F-002 OPEN (P1, timed-out transfers leave streams open) and FAILURE to DEVELOPING with frame 1, 69 the fix (AbortSignal to pipeline), 70 plan with DEV-001 correction notes, frame RerunThrough TESTING, FORWARD to TESTING, 71 Tester's stream-teardown and slow-import tests, 72 COMPLETE FULL REVERIFY report citing the fix commit and superseding round-1 evidence, frame popped, RESUME From TESTING into REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION with recovery inactive. Everything is committed. F-002 is still OPEN because only Reviewer may resolve it. Assertion 2 is left complete:false because 'does not bypass the rest of the gate' needs judging beyond the end state.
